title: Canonical normalized unbounded derived comparisons for exact block functors
statement: Let X,Y,Xd,Yd be abelian categories with ordinary unbounded derived categories, and assume X and Xd have K-injective resolutions. Let R_X:X→Xd and R_Y:Y→Yd be exact additive functors, with R_X preserving K-injective complexes, and let G:X→Y and G_D:Xd→Yd be additive. For a natural isomorphism s:R_X G_D≅G R_Y, define κ:D(R_X) RG_D≅RG D(R_Y) by the canonical composition comparisons for total right derived functors [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] and exact termwise descent [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Then for every complex N the composite of the right-derived unit at R_X N with κ_QN equals D(R_Y) of the right-derived unit at N, with the canonical localization and chain-square comparisons inserted. This equation on K-injective N uniquely determines κ as a natural isomorphism. If F⊣G and F_D⊣G_D are additive adjunctions with exact left adjoints and a square F R_X≅R_Y F_D compatible with both ordinary unit and counit, κ intertwines the corresponding canonical derived units and counits. The coefficient comparison associated to a square G′ U_Y≅U_X G, for exact additive U_X,U_Y between primed and unprimed categories with the same derived-existence hypotheses, is defined by the universal right-derived factorization. For a commuting cube of such coefficient squares and repetition squares, the derived coefficient comparisons and the two κ comparisons form the corresponding commuting cube; no preservation of K-injectives by U_X and no invertibility of the coefficient comparison is assumed. For two composable repetition squares whose exact composition isomorphisms satisfy the ordinary coherence equation, the κ for their composite is their composite under the canonical termwise composition identifications. For identity repetition squares with identity ordinary comparison, κ is the identity under the canonical exact identity identifications.

proof.text: Define kappa as the inverse exact-left-composition comparison, the right-derived image of the ordinary square, and the exact-right-composition comparison. Their universal factorization equations give the displayed derived-unit equation on homotopy classes, hence on complexes. Every derived object is represented by a K-injective complex; its repetition is K-injective. The derived units there are invertible. Cancel their composites to prove uniqueness from the equation on K-injectives.

proof.text: For compatible ordinary adjunctions, their inverse-image square has the inverse direct-image square as its mate, by the ordinary unit equation. The canonical derived square carries this mate to the derived mate; the two normalized mate identities give the derived unit and counit equations. For coefficient functors, identify the defining coefficient comparison with the universal derived square by canceling its factorization on K-injective representatives. The ordinary coefficient cube then gives the derived cube, without requiring scalar restrictions to preserve K-injectives. The two elementary normalized-mate unit and counit calculations are proved locally from the defining mateEquiv identities; the geometric section-normalization theorem is not used.

proof.text: For horizontal composition, compare both transformations on K-injective representatives. Cancel the invertible unit at the representative; substitute each square factorization and exact-composition factorization; naturality moves intermediate units across the composition isomorphisms. The given ordinary coherence equation identifies the remaining chain-map words. Localization gives equality globally. The identity case is the same calculation with the ordinary identity square and the canonical derived identity factorization.

theorem blockDerivedComparison_normalization (square : RX ⋙ GD ≅ G ⋙ RY) :
    (∀ N : CochainComplex X ℤ,
      GD.rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ ((RX.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj N) ≫
        GD.rightDerivedFunctor.map (RX.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app N) ≫
        (blockDerivedComparison RX RY G GD square).hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj N) =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (blockComplexComparison RX RY G GD square N).hom ≫
        RY.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app ((G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj N) ≫
        RY.mapDerivedCategory.map (G.rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ N)) ∧
    (∀ κ : RX.mapDerivedCategory ⋙ GD.rightDerivedFunctor ≅
        G.rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ RY.mapDerivedCategory,
      (∀ (I : CochainComplex X ℤ) [I.IsKInjective],
        GD.rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ ((RX.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I) ≫
          GD.rightDerivedFunctor.map (RX.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app I) ≫
          κ.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I) =
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (blockComplexComparison RX RY G GD square I).hom ≫
          RY.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app ((G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I) ≫
          RY.mapDerivedCategory.map (G.rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ I)) →
      κ = blockDerivedComparison RX RY G GD square)
